title: Cyrus and the Contact
premise: August Galloway walked away from hostage negotiation after a botched exchange left a teenage informant dead, and she's spent three years hiding under her late mother's name in a coastal town. When a burner phone rings with the voice of Cyrus, the informant she failed, alive and claiming to be a defector trapped in a portside safehouse, August realizes someone is using her guilt as bait to flush out a mole inside her old agency. She assembles an unlikely crew—a retired handler, a forger, and the dead girl's sister—to extract Cyrus while untangling who set the trap. In the end August trades herself for Cyrus, exposes the mole on live frequency, and inherits not just her mother's hidden estate but a found family willing to burn their old lives to stand beside her.
about_author: Ansel Galloway is the pen name of a former crisis-line volunteer who spent a decade listening to strangers talk each other back from ledges. They write thrillers about people whose jobs require them to stay calm while everything burns.

chapters.title: The Phone That Shouldn't Ring
chapters.summary: August's POV. Three years into quiet exile, August tends her mother's neglected orchard until a burner phone buried in her mother's toolbox rings with Cyrus's voice—the boy she believes died because of her. He begs for extraction from a portside safehouse before Friday. The emotional beat is vertigo: grief cracking open into hope, then suspicion, as August notices the call's timing matches her mother's death anniversary too neatly.

chapters.title: Everyone Owes Someone
chapters.summary: Alternating POV between August and Vera, the dead informant's sister now working forgery in the city. August recruits her old handler Marsh and confronts Vera with the impossible news; Vera joins not out of forgiveness but to see the body herself. They map the safehouse and discover the 'defector' file contains August's own sealed failure report. The beat is reluctant alliance—wounds reopened, trust bartered, the crew forming around shared debt.

chapters.title: Friday Comes Early
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV interleaved with the extraction. The team breaches the safehouse during a staged customs inspection, but Cyrus reveals he called August deliberately: he recognized the mole's voice on his handlers' line and knew only she would believe him. Ambush springs—the mole anticipated them—and Marsh takes a bullet covering the retreat. The climax beat is betrayal inverted into sacrifice, August choosing to stay behind as collateral so Cyrus and Vera can run.

chapters.title: What the Dead Leave Us
chapters.summary: August's POV. Held in the safehouse, August negotiates her own life using the one thing she never surrendered: the recorded proof of the mole's voice, broadcast agency-wide by Vera from outside. Cyrus returns against orders to walk her out through the burning dockyard. Weeks later, at her mother's revealed estate, the four of them scatter ashes and unpack the inheritance—not money, but a network of the discarded, and a new phone that only they can answer.
